messages:
anna_sec: hitting AccessDenied when a cross-account worker role tries to kms:Decrypt our data key. CloudTrail shows KMS\u003aDecrypt denied. anyone see this pattern before?

devon_infra: is this the assume-role -> call KMS from the target account flow? usually a key policy mismatch or a session policy boundary. any snippets of the key policy?

anna_sec: yup, flow is: service-account in acct A assumes role in acct B, then calls KMS (acct B). key is in acct B. key policy currently only allows principals from acct B -> "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/data-plane".

jordan_sre: two quick things to check: 1) session policy / permissions boundary on the assumed role might be stripping kms:Decrypt. 2) encryption context mismatch will also give AccessDenied.

matt_ops: can you paste the exact CloudTrail error entry? also do a local repro with aws cli after assume-role. example: 
```
creds=$(aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/data-plane --role-session-name debug)
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo $creds | jq -r .Credentials.AccessKeyId) ...
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222333444555:key/xxxx --encryption-context FileId=123
```
if that errors, run `aws kms get-key-policy` and `aws iam get-role --role-name data-plane`

deploy-bot: CloudTrail: EventName=Decrypt, ErrorCode=AccessDeniedException, UserIdentityArn=arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/bridge-role/session123, Resource=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222333444555:key/xxxx

devon_infra: note: KMS key policy should reference the IAM role ARN (the role itself), not the assumed-role session ARN. But also the *role's effective permissions* are the intersection of role policy + session policy, so a session policy could be the culprit.

anna_sec: found this: the service that assumes the role is passing a very restrictive session policy when calling AssumeRole. the role policy allows kms:Decrypt but the session policy only allows s3. so result = no kms.

jordan_sre: yep that explains it. alternative fixes: a) relax the session policy or b) create an explicit KMS grant for the role principal (arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/data-plane) so KMS allows decrypt regardless of key policy conditions. grants also have granteePrincipal that can be the role. run: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/app-key --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/data-plane --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey
```
but grants expire or must be tracked.

matt_ops: also double-check any key policy conditions using kms:ViaService or aws:SourceAccount. we had a condition that restricted calls to Lambda service principal and that blocked assume-role callers when they weren't coming from lambda.

anna_sec: good catch — our key policy had a condition: "aws:PrincipalIsAWSService": false and we also had a mismatched aws:SourceAccount. removed the restrictive condition for the role and re-tested.

devon_infra: final checklist that fixed similar incidents for us: 
- ensure key policy has a Statement allowing the role ARN (not assumed session) to use kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey
- confirm no session policy / permissions boundary are removing kms actions
- verify encryption context used in Decrypt matches the one used at Encrypt
- consider a short-lived grant if you can't change key policy (and track lifecycle)
- check CloudTrail KMS event for encryptionContext mismatch vs policy denial

anna_sec: applied policy change and reprobed with CLI, success: `Decrypt OK` 

matt_ops: logged remediation in ticket #SEC-4021, adding a note to run an org-wide scan for other keys that have restrictive source-account/service conditions.

jordan_sre: 👍 also add a tiny playbook: if AccessDenied, check (1) session policy (2) key policy principal (3) encryption context (4) active grants — in that order. saves time.

anna_sec: thanks all — saved our rollout window. :rocket:
